html:
The Bhakra Dam is a concrete dam on the Sutlej River in the Himalayan foothills of north India, built from 1948 to 1963. Its water and power fed the Green Revolution in Punjab and Haryana.

It is one of the tallest gravity dams in the world, about 226 metres high. Canals from the dam irrigate farms across Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan, and its power station lights much of the north. An American engineer, Harvey Slocum, a veteran of big dams in the United States like the Hoover Dam, led the building.

The dam was a pet project of the new state. Jawaharlal Nehru called such projects the temples of modern India. It answered a need created by the Partition of India, which left most of the old canal lands of the Punjab canal colonies in Pakistan. Under the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 the Sutlej went to India.

The reservoir flooded many villages, and the people moved out waited decades for fair land. Later critics of big dams pointed to Bhakra too, but it remains a symbol of India's early planning era.
sum: The Bhakra Dam is a concrete dam on the Sutlej River in the Himalayan foothills of north India, built from 1948 to 1963. Its water and power fed the Green Revolution in Punjab and Haryana.
